newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks seen pressured by rate jitters.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks seen pressured by rate jitters.

text.p: Interest rate jitters are expected to continue weighing on Hong Kong stocks on Friday, ahead of U.S. August employment data due later, analysts said.

"Today I am not that encouraged by the jobs data that will be coming out tonight and therefore I think investors will be very nervous and stay on the sidelines and possibly even sell down property counters further," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"It seems like the index could drop again today. Wall Street fell overnight and the bond yield is higher," he added.
The Hang Seng fell 36.44 points on Thursday to 11,040.51.
Overnight, the Dow Industrials fell 49.94 points to 5,606.96 and the U.S. long bond shed 20/32 to yield 7.15 percent.

"No one is really going to start wanting to put money into the market ahead of the jobs figures tonight so the chances are that Hong Kong is going a little bit lower," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
"It's all pretty low volume at the moment," he added.
